reason: Earlier native GEMV microbenchmarks inherited the default dedicated compute queue, whereas qualified TP5 uses the graphics-capable compute family. Cold-vs-stream anomalies also require sustained workload warmup.
control: Same actual native Vulkan backend code, fixed200ms workload warmup, GGML_VK_ALLOW_GRAPHICS_QUEUE=1 matching production, MMVQdisabled, resident and>128MiB streaming addresses, no clock writes.
limits: These are isolated native contractions, not necessarily the fused production region. Timings include host graph submission/synchronization amortized over repeated operations; do not rename them pure GPU hardware lower bounds or add a second dispatch overhead. Use actual fused MoE service for the gate/up region instead of these generic proxies.
independence: No model-request time or fitted residual enters this calibration. Every cost replacing a matrix or region must also remove that region's prior logical-weight estimate.
